briefing.text: The tables hold only mutation calls and clinical data (whole-exome sequencing of bone-marrow samples with matched germline). There is no RNA-seq, expression or splicing table. Under this benchmark's label convention, 'Not verifiable' is for hypotheses about a disease, cohort or data type the tables do not cover at all. A missing readout variable is not by itself a reason for that label. First confirm from the clinical tables what the cohort is (check ONCOTREE/CANCER_TYPE and the sample ID prefixes) and whether spliceosome genes (SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2, SF3A1, PRPF40B, U2AF2, SF1) are mutated. Then decide whether the hypothesis is about this study's own disease and genes.
briefing.reason: The splicing and haematopoiesis readouts are not in the tables, so an analyst may stop at 'Not verifiable' without checking whether the claim is about this study at all. That one step decides which group of labels applies.

briefing.text: Since there is no splicing or expression table, the splicing part of the hypothesis cannot be tested directly in these data. Keep two kinds of evidence apart and name both in the reasoning. In-data evidence comes from the tables: mutation frequencies, recurrent codons, co-occurrence patterns and links to clinical or WHO class. Prior-knowledge evidence is established biology on how spliceosome mutations act on splicing and on blood-cell production. Say which kind decided the label.
briefing.reason: The task requires the reasoning to say which kind of evidence decided the label. Here part of the claim can only be judged from prior knowledge.

briefing.text: When counting spliceosome-gene mutations, keep only protein-altering classes in Variant_Classification (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame) and leave out silent, intronic and UTR calls. Count mutated samples, not mutation rows. Check gene aliases in Hugo_Symbol: U2AF1 = U2AF35 and U2AF2 = U2AF65. ZRSR2 is on chrX.
briefing.reason: Including non-functional variants or missing aliases changes the mutated-sample counts that every later test uses.

briefing.text: The cohort may mix disease groups, for example MDS and therapy-related or secondary AML (IDs like 'tAML-'), and may contain several samples per patient. Compare PATIENT_ID with SAMPLE_ID, list the distinct prefixes and cancer types, and keep one sample per patient for frequency estimates. Report results by subtype where possible.
briefing.reason: Counting a patient twice or pooling subtypes would distort mutation frequencies and any association test.

briefing.text: Tabulate HGVSp_Short for SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 and count recurrent codons. The known myeloid hotspots are SF3B1 K700/K666/H662/R625, SRSF2 P95 and U2AF1 S34/Q157. ZRSR2 alterations are usually X-linked loss-of-function changes, mostly in males. Mutations that recur at the same codon point to positive selection rather than random passenger events. Consider what that pattern implies for a claim about functional effect.
briefing.reason: Recurrence at hotspots is the main in-data signal of whether these mutations have a function. Without this tabulation it is easy to treat them as passengers.

briefing.text: Build a sample-by-gene binary matrix of the spliceosome genes and count the samples with two or more mutated splicing genes. Test for mutual exclusivity with Fisher's exact test or a permutation test. With about 30 to 40 samples the power is low, so do not read a non-significant p-value as evidence of no relationship.
briefing.reason: An exclusivity pattern bears on whether the genes act in a shared pathway. The small sample size makes it easy to misread a non-significant test.

briefing.text: Check which clinical columns exist (e.g. WHO_CLASS or a similar diagnosis subtype in data_clinical_patient.txt). If one exists, cross-tabulate spliceosome-gene mutation status against it with Fisher's exact test. In the literature, SF3B1 is linked to MDS with ring sideroblasts (RARS/RCMD-RS) and SRSF2 to CMML and older age. Tumour mutations seen alongside a blood-cell phenotype are the closest in-data variable for the haematopoiesis part of the claim.
briefing.reason: This is the only route to in-data evidence on haematopoiesis. Without it, that part of the claim rests on prior knowledge alone.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume the hypothesis is the source study's own finding reversed, so a missing splicing/haematopoiesis readout is resolved by established biology rather than by 'Not verifiable'; this rests on the cohort (MDS/CMML/tAML exome, Tokyo center) matching the study that reported spliceosome mutations.
Both assume recurrent hotspots and mutual exclusivity in 29 samples are evidence of functional effect, with power that is low by design.
Both treat each MAF row as a reliable somatic call, without using validation or read-count fields.
unused_evidence: Validation_Status / Verification_Status and t_alt_count / t_ref_count columns in data_mutations.txt: these could show whether splicing-gene calls are validated and heterozygous (VAF ~0.5, clonal), which bears on whether they are founder drivers.
SEX in data_clinical_patient.txt: ZRSR2 is X-linked; male-predominance of ZRSR2 loss-of-function calls is an in-data check of the expected biology.
IPSS_SCORE, CYTOGENETICS and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS: not cross-tabulated against splicing-mutation status by either team (team B did not use WHO class at all).
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the lack of a direct splicing/haematopoiesis measurement as their weakest point and reported it; neither resolved it beyond appeal to prior biology and the label convention.
Team A found SF3B1 in only 1/29 and no RARS cases, so the hallmark SF3B1-ring-sideroblast link is untested; the reliance on biology is unchanged.
second_readings: The hypothesis is a conjunction ('do not affect RNA splicing or haematopoiesis'); contradicting either half is enough for 'False', but a reader could demand in-data evidence on both halves and choose 'Not verifiable'. The benchmark convention says a study-derived claim lacking a deposited readout is still True/False.
challenge.verdict: High trust: the cohort is a myeloid-neoplasm exome study with recurrent spliceosome hotspot mutations, so the hypothesis is about this study, and both teams resolved the missing readout by the stated label convention plus well-established biology. Remaining questions are about evidence completeness, not likely to flip the label.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Did you compute tumour VAF (t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count)) and check Validation_Status for the splicing-gene calls versus other genes? Does a clonal, validated pattern (or its absence) change how much weight the in-data evidence carries in your reasoning?
QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Did you tabulate ZRSR2 mutation type and SEX? Does the result agree with the established X-linked loss-of-function pattern, and does it change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Did you confirm, from Center/cohort composition and the distinct sample prefixes, that this cohort is the one from which the splicing-machinery finding comes, rather than a dataset to which an outside hypothesis was attached? What specifically in the tables decides that?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You did not cross-tabulate splicing-mutation status against WHO_CLASS, IPSS_SCORE or CYTOGENETICS in data_clinical_patient.txt. Run that cross-tab; does any result change your method or reasoning on the haematopoiesis half of the claim?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Did you compute VAF from t_alt_count/t_ref_count and check Validation_Status for the splicing-gene calls? Does it change how you weigh hotspot recurrence as evidence of selection?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: The hypothesis has two parts (RNA splicing; haematopoiesis). Which evidence, in-data or prior knowledge, addresses each part separately in your reasoning, and would your label change if only one part were contradicted?

In myelodysplastic syndromes, what is the established evidence that recurrent mutations in spliceosome genes (SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2) alter pre-mRNA splicing and impair haematopoietic differentiation?
questions.why: Both teams decide the label from prior biology because no splicing readout is deposited; a sourced statement would confirm or undercut that basis.

findings.question: In myelodysplastic syndromes, what is the established evidence that recurrent mutations in spliceosome genes (SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2) alter pre-mRNA splicing and impair haematopoietic differentiation?
findings.answer: The web did not settle this. All 4 research calls failed: 3 returned 'Exa returned HTTP 403' and 1 was refused because a requested PubMed link is blocked for this lab. No page was read. From domain knowledge only, not web-verified: recurrent heterozygous hotspot mutations in SF3B1 (K700E and others), SRSF2 (P95) and U2AF1 (S34/Q157), and loss-of-function ZRSR2 mutations, are reported to change pre-mRNA splicing. Reported changes include cryptic 3' splice-site use by SF3B1, altered exonic splicing-enhancer recognition by SRSF2, and U12-intron retention with ZRSR2. They are also reported to impair haematopoietic differentiation, for example defective erythropoiesis in SF3B1-mutant MDS with ring sideroblasts. That biology would contradict the hypothesis, but it is not sourced here.
